3 MVC No.1245/2021  SCCH-25  JUDGMENT

This is a Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the Death of B.Sankarappa who died in a road traffic accident dated 29.01.2020.

2. The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, on 29.01.2020 morning at about 6.45 am the deceased B.Sankarappa went as Driver of Tractor of 1 st Respondent bearing No.AP03AQ3150 for taking humus at Chilakavaripalli Village at about 10.00am on enroute due to crossing of buffaloes, the deceased applied brakes at turning, as a result of which fell down and sustained right side head injury.

Immediately he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Madnapalle for treatment, but the duty medical officer examined him and declared that he was brought dead due to fatal injuries and conducted autopsy on the dead body and issued the PM certificate.
SCCH-25 3

. It is further case of the Petitioners that the 1 st petitioner who is the wife of the deceased had lost her consortium at the age of 34 years and petitioners No.2 to 4 who are the minor daughters of the deceased have lost their beloved father and during the lifetime of the deceased he was working as Driver of Tractor of 1st Respondent and getting salary of Rs.3,300/ per month.

The accident is purely has occurred out of the use of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP03AQ3150, the Station House Officer of Punganur Urban police have registered a case in their Cr.No.19/2020 punishable u/Sec.304(A) of IPC.

The 1 st respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the Smt.Roopa vs Buvaneswari on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190683862/
2 insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to them.
4. In response to summons issued by this court, the Respondents have appeared through their respective SCCH-25 counsels, but the respondent No.2 alone has filed separate written statement.

5. The Respondent No.2 insurance company in the written statement have denied the averments made in the petition as false, admitted issuance of policy but their liability if any is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that the petition is not maintainable as on account of rash and negligent act of the deceased himself the accident taken place and the claim for the death of a person who himself was responsible for the accident is not maintainable u/Sec.163A of MV Act as held by the Hon'ble HC (DB) in the case of Appaji and Ors., Vs. M.Krishna & Anr., reported in 2004 ACJ 1289.

sentences.text: Since the deceased himself was driving the alleged vehicle bearing No.AP03 AQ3150 at the time of accident and hence he cannot be considered as a third party and hence the petition is itself not maintainable.
Further submitted that this Tribunal has got no jurisdiction to try this petition.
Granting SCCH-25 compensation for one's own negligence is wrong and erroneous.

The present petition is also not maintainable under Section 163A in the facts and circumstances of the present case as the provisions of Section 163A are only applicable to Third party as these provisions fall under Chapter XI (Section 145 to Section 164) of the MV Act, 188.
The very heading/title of chapter XI (covering Section 145 to 164) is "INSURANCE OF MOTOR VEHICLE AGAINST THIRD PARTY RISTK".
The first party is Insurance Company i.e. insurer and the second party is the insured i.e. owner (insured).

Therefore,
the provision of Section 163A apply only to for a person victim other than the Insurer and the insured and his driver/agent.

Since the claimant is not a Third aprty under the Motor Vehicles Act and or under the requirement of Insurance policy (Section 147 of MV Act), therefore, they have no liability and petitioner is not maintainable.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?

4. What Order or Award?

My finding to the above issues are as follows: SCCH-25 Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final order, for the Following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Wife and the Petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased - Sri.Sankarappa.
In this regard, the Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the first Petitioner as PW.1.
The PW.1 has specifically deposed this relationship in her chiefexamination.

Apart from that, to prove the relationship the Petitioners have also produced notarized copies of Aadhar Cards of the petitioners and the deceased, pension card and DL of the deceased as per Exs.P.6 to 8.

There is no contrary to Smt.Roopa vs Buvaneswari on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190683862/
4 these documents from the respondents.

In Ex.P.6 in the Aadhar Cards of the petitioner No.1 her husband's name is mentioned as SCCH-25 B.Shankarappa and in the Aadhar Cards of the Petitioner Nos.2 to 4 their father's name is mentioned as B.Shankarappa and in the Aadhar Card of the deceased his father's name is mentioned as B.Obulappa.
In the same manner.
In Ex.P.7 pension card of petitioner No.1 her husband's name is mentioned as B.Shankarappa and also in Ex.P.8 DL of the deceased his father's name is mentioned as B.Obulappa.
Further, these documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondent No.2.
The Respondent No.2 has not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.

As such,
there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are the wife and children of the SCCH-25 deceased B.Sankarappa.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2: The Petitioners to prove their case have examined first Petitioner as PW.1 and produced Exs.P.1 to P.5.

The PW.1 has specifically deposed in her evidence that her husband was on duty as a Tractor Driver bearing Reg.No.AP03AQ 3150 which belongs to the 1st respondent and the Tractor was loaded with cattle fodder at Edigapalli in order to unload the same at Chilakavaripalli Village which was driven by her husband slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, while so proceeding at about 10.00am, reached at Chilakavaripalli Village turning suddenly buffaloes crossed the road and her husband applied brake at turning, lost control, fell down and sustained severe bleeding injuries on right side head and caused the accident result of which her husband was expired.
The Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.4 is the First SCCH-25 information filed by the wife of the deceased Smt.Battala Roopa, Exs.2, 3 and 5 are the PM certificate, final report and inqeust report.

The Respondent No.2, on the other side being the insurer of the vehicle involved in the accident has denied the case of the petitioners as false and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable.
12. It is pertinent to note that the present petition is filed under section 163A and not under section 166 of IMV Act.

In the proceedings under section 163A of IMV Act, question to be considered by this Tribunal is whether there is involvement of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed and not whether there is a rash or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the said vehicle.

The aspect of negligence or contributory negligence has no role to play in deciding the question of the entitlement for compensation.
13.

Section 163A of I.M.V.Act stipulates that, SCCH-25 "not withstanding anything contained in this act or in nay other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in case of death or permanent disablement due to the accident arising out of use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the second schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim as the case may be".
14.

sentences.text: In para No. 8 of the said judgment, it is observed that, "it is clear that grant of compensation under section 163A of the act on the basis of the structured formula is in the nature of final award and the adjudication there under is required to be made without any requirement of any poof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicle/s involved in the accident.

This is made explicit by section 163(a)
(2).

Though the aforesaid section of the act does not specifically exclude the possible defense of insurer based on the negligence of the claimant as contemplated by section 140(4), to permit such defense to be introduced by the insurer and or to understand the provision of SCCH-25 section 163A of the act to be contemplating any such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of section 163A of the act, namely final compensation with a limited time frame on the basis of the structured formula to overcome situation where the claims of the compensation on the basis of the fault liability was taking an unduly long time.

In fact, to understand the section 163A of the act to permit the insurer to raise the defense of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under section 163A of the act at par with the proceedings under section 166 of the act which would not only be self contradictory, but also defeat the very legislative intention".
15.

The Hon'ble Supreme court in the year 2004 itself in a decision reported in (2004) 5 SCC 385 rendered in Deepal Girihsbhai Soni and Ors Vs United India Insurance co, ltd., held that "section 163A covers the cases where negligence is even on part of the victim excluding the defense of contributory negligence".

In AIR 2017 SC 5710, wherein at para 8 it is observed as under;
"8.From the above discussion, it is clear that grant of compensation under Section 163A of the Act on the basis of the structured formula is in the nature of a final award and the adjudication thereunder is required to be made without any requirement of any proof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicles(s) involved in the accident.
This is made explicit by Section 163A(2).

Though the aforesaid section of the Act does not specifically exclude a possible defence of the Insurer based on the negligence of the claimant as contemplated by Section 140(4), to permit such defence to be introduced by the Insurer and/or to understand the SCCH-25 provisions of Section 163A of the Act to be contemplating any such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of Section 163A of the Act,
namely, final compensation within a limited time frame on the basis of the structured formula to overcome situations where the claims of compensation on the basis of fault liability was taking an unduly long time.

In fact, to understand Section 163A of the Act to permit the Insurer to raise the defence of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under Section 163A of the Act as par with the proceeding under Section 166 of the Act which would not only be selfcontradictory but also defeat the very legislative intention."

17. In (2020) 7 SCC 386 the Hon'ble Apex Court held at para 10 to 12 as under;
"10. Section 163A reads as follows:

sentences.text: Special provisions as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis.

(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle,
compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
Explanation.
For the purposes of this sub section, "permanent disability" shall have the same meaning and extent as in the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923).

(2) In any claim for compensation under subsection (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to SCCH-25 any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person.
(3) The Central Government may, keeping in view the cost of living by notification in the Official Gazette, from time to time amend the Second Schedule."

11. A perusal of this provision would show that Shri Sahoo is correct in stating that the claimant need not plead or establish that the death in respect of which the claim was made, was due to any negligence or default of the owner of the vehicle or of any other person.

12. In this view of the matter, it is not relevant that the person insured must be the driver of the vehicle but may well have been riding with somebody else driving a vehicle which resulted in the death of the person driving the vehicle.

The High Court, therefore, is clearly wrong in stating that it was necessary under Section 163A to prove that somebody else was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently, as a result of which, the death of the victim would take place."
18.

I have perused the decisions relied upon by the counsel for the respondent No.2 but they are not applicable to the present case in view of Hon'ble Apex Court decision rendered by Three Judge of S.C. in the case of Chandrakanta Tiwari.

I have perused the decisions relied upon by the counsel for the petitioners and they are aptly applicable to the present case about the maintainability of SCCH-25 petitioner u/Sec.163A and award of compensation under structured formula.

Therefore,
in view of above provision of law and decisions of Hon'ble Apex court and Hon'ble H.C., it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under section 163A of the act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal and same is need not be proved by the claimants.
All that has to be considered by this Tribunal is whether vehicle against which the claim made is involved in the accident or not.
19. In this case, it is pertinent to note that nowhere in the written statement the Respondent No.2 have seriously denied the involvement of the vehicle bearing No.AP03AQ3150 in the accident.
On the other hand, it is contended that it was occurred due the negligence of the deceased himself.
Smt.Roopa vs Buvaneswari on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190683862/

8 In the cross examination also, the Respondents have not disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident seriously but only it is suggested that it was occurred due to the negligence of the SCCH-25 deceased himself.

Though, the Respondent No.2 has got examined ITS Legal Manager as RW.1 and produced authorization letter and true copy of policy with terms and conditions but the RW.1 has not disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle in his evidence.

Therefore, the very contention of the Respondent/Insurance Company that the deceased was driving his vehicle with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident himself proves that the vehicle bearing No.AP03AQ3150 was involved in the accident.
There is no other proof required to establish the involvement of the vehicle bearing No.AP03 AQ3150 in the accident.
20. Despite this, the documents produced by the Petitioners as per Exs.P.1 to P.5(a) are all public documents which have got initial presumptive value under law.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of the PW.1, RW.1, coupled with Exs.P.1 to P.5(a), this Tribunal is of the opinion that there was an accident by involvement of SCCH-25 Tractor bearing Reg. No.AP03 AQ3150 and result of such accident deceased Sankarappa has sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to those injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the affirmative.
21. Issue No. 3:
The PW.1 has specifically deposed before this court that she being the wife, other Petitioners being the minor children of the deceased were entirely depending upon the earning of the deceased.
But due to the untimely death of the deceased, they are suffering from mental agony and financial difficulties.
Therefore, they are all considered as the Dependants of the deceased.

Under such circumstances, the Petitioner No.1, the wife of the deceased and the Petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are the minor children of the deceased shall be treated as dependents of the deceased - Sankrappa.

This court while discussing the issue No.2 has already come to the conclusion that the accident was occurred due to involvement of the Tractor which resulted SCCH-25 in the death of the deceased - Sankrappa.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of the deceased.
Monthly income 22.
The Petitioners have averred that, deceased was a Driver of the Tractor under the 1st Respondent and earning a sum of Rs.3,300/ per month.
In this regard, the Petitioner No.1 has entered into witness box and stated that deceased was earning an income of Rs.3,300/ per annum.
The Respondent No.2, in the cross examination except denial have not suggested what else is the income of the Petitioner if not Rs.39,600/ per annum.
The Respondent No.2 has also not placed any contrary document on record.
Under these circumstances, it appears, it would be justified if notional income of the Petitioner is considered as Rs.39,600/ per annum for calculating the loss of dependency.
Hence, his income is considered as SCCH-25 Rs.39,600/ per annum.

As such,
Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation: Age of the deceased 23.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.6.
As per this document as on the date of accident on 29.01.2020, his age was 40 years.
Ex.P.6 document is a public document and it has got initial presumptive value under law.
There are no contrary documents placed by the Respondents.

Therefore, this Tribunal has to Smt.Roopa vs Buvaneswari on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190683862/
9 reply upon the said document.
Therefore, relying upon the said document, the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is considered as 40 years.

24. As per the amendment brought to the second schedule by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways which notification published in the official Gazette dated SCCH-25 22.05.2018 the compensation payable in case of death shall be Rs.5,00,000/.

The Gazette notification reads as under;
"THE SECOND SCHEDULE (See Section 163A) SCHEDULE FOR COMPENSATION FOR THIRD PARTY FATAL ACCIDENT/INJURY CASES CLAIMS (a) Fatal Accidents:
Compensation payable in case of Death shall be five lakh rupees.
(b) Accidents resulting in permanent disability:
Compensation payable shall be [Rs.5,00,000/ x percentage disability as per Schedule I of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923)]:
(c) Accidents resulting in minor injury:
A fixed compensation of twenty five thousand rupees shall be payable:
On and from the date of 1 st day of January, 2019 the amount of compensation specified in the clauses (a) to (c) of paragraph (1) shall stand increased by 5 percent annually.
This notification shall come into form on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette."
25. Therefore, the monthly or annual income and age of the deceased is immaterial in view of aforesaid amendment.

Further it is also stated that On and from the date of 1st day of January, 2019 the amount of SCCH-25 compensation specified in the clauses (a) to (c) of paragraph (1) shall stand increased by 5 percent annually.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,25,000/ as fixed compensation as per the above amendment published in the Gazette Notification.

Accordingly, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,25,000/ alongwith interest @
6% per annum from the date of petition till date of deposit.

As discussed above the Respondent No.2  insurer have not proved their defence.
There is no dispute with regard to existence of policy as on the date of accident.
Therefore the respondents 1 and 2 being RC owner and insurer are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, as the policy is existed and hence the respondent No.2 is to indemnify the respondent No.1 insured and directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The Petitioners has claimed an amount of Rs.50,00,000/, but SCCH-25 they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,25,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Therefore the Petition is allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.4: For the reasons and discussions made above and findings to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,25,000/ (Rupees Five Lakhs Twenty Five Thousand only) alongwith interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the SCCH-25 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The accident is purely has occurred out of the use of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP03AQ3150, the Station House Officer of Punganur Urban police have registered a case in their Cr.No.19/2020 punishable u/Sec.304(A) of IPC.
5. The Respondent No.2 insurance company in the written statement have denied the averments made in the petition as false, admitted issuance of policy but their liability if any is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that the petition is not maintainable as on account of rash and negligent act of the deceased himself the accident taken place and the claim for the death of a person who himself was responsible for the accident is not maintainable u/Sec.163A of MV Act as held by the Hon'ble HC (DB) in the case of Appaji and Ors., Vs. M.Krishna & Anr., reported in 2004 ACJ 1289.
Since the deceased himself was driving the alleged vehicle bearing No.AP03 AQ3150 at the time of accident and hence he cannot be considered as a third party and hence the petition is itself not maintainable.
Granting SCCH-25 compensation for one's own negligence is wrong and erroneous.
The present petition is also not maintainable under Section 163A in the facts and circumstances of the present case as the provisions of Section 163A are only applicable to Third party as these provisions fall under Chapter XI (Section 145 to Section 164) of the MV Act, 188.
The first party is Insurance Company i.e. insurer and the second party is the insured i.e. owner (insured).
Therefore,
the provision of Section 163A apply only to for a person victim other than the Insurer and the insured and his driver/agent.
Since the claimant is not a Third aprty under the Motor Vehicles Act and or under the requirement of Insurance policy (Section 147 of MV Act), therefore, they have no liability and petitioner is not maintainable.
opennyai_summary.issue:
On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.B.Sankarappa?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.B.Sankarappa was died on account of RTA took place at Chilakavaripalli Village, while driving Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP03 AQ 3150, dated 29.01.2020 at about 10.00am?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
4. What Order or Award?
Smt.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the proceedings under section 163A of IMV Act, question to be considered by this Tribunal is whether there is involvement of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed and not whether there is a rash or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the said vehicle.
The aspect of negligence or contributory negligence has no role to play in deciding the question of the entitlement for compensation.
13.
Therefore,
in view of above provision of law and decisions of Hon'ble Apex court and Hon'ble H.C., it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under section 163A of the act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal and same is need not be proved by the claimants.
All that has to be considered by this Tribunal is whether vehicle against which the claim made is involved in the accident or not.
19. In this case, it is pertinent to note that nowhere in the written statement the Respondent No.2 have seriously denied the involvement of the vehicle bearing No.AP03AQ3150 in the accident.
There is no other proof required to establish the involvement of the vehicle bearing No.AP03 AQ3150 in the accident.
Therefore, they are all considered as the Dependants of the deceased.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioner No.1, the wife of the deceased and the Petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are the minor children of the deceased shall be treated as dependents of the deceased - Sankrappa.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of the deceased.
The Petitioners have averred that, deceased was a Driver of the Tractor under the 1st Respondent and earning a sum of Rs.3,300/ per month.
Hence, his income is considered as SCCH-25 Rs.39,600/ per annum.
Ex.P.6 document is a public document and it has got initial presumptive value under law.
There are no contrary documents placed by the Respondents.
opennyai_summary.decision:
24. As per the amendment brought to the second schedule by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways which notification published in the official Gazette dated SCCH-25 22.05.2018 the compensation payable in case of death shall be Rs.5,00,000/.
This notification shall come into form on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette."
25. Therefore, the monthly or annual income and age of the deceased is immaterial in view of aforesaid amendment.
Further it is also stated that On and from the date of 1st day of January, 2019 the amount of SCCH-25 compensation specified in the clauses (a) to (c) of paragraph (1) shall stand increased by 5 percent annually.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,25,000/ as fixed compensation as per the above amendment published in the Gazette Notification.
Accordingly, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,25,000/ alongwith interest @
6% per annum from the date of petition till date of deposit.
Therefore the respondents 1 and 2 being RC owner and insurer are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Petitioners has claimed an amount of Rs.50,00,000/, but SCCH-25 they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,25,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Therefore the Petition is allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.4: For the reasons and discussions made above and findings to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,25,000/ (Rupees Five Lakhs Twenty Five Thousand only) alongwith interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the SCCH-25 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.2 - insurer is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.
On deposit of the award amount and interest, 5% each shall be deposited in the names of the petitioner Nos.2 to 4 in any N/S Bank till they attain the age of majority and remaining entire compensation shall be released in favour of the petitioner No.1 with proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
SCCH-25 Draw Award accordingly.
